# SHIFROM

> SHIFROM is an open-source (AGPL-3.0-or-later), end-to-end encrypted messenger for Android, built for hostile networks: networks that filter, throttle or block traffic. No phone number, email or real name is required. Status: Alpha 2. Maintained by Willen LLC (Wyoming, USA).

Important qualifiers that travel with every claim below:

- SHIFROM is in Alpha 2. Source builds and tagged development snapshots are on GitHub; there is no public end-user APK or open beta yet. Public builds come with Beta.
- The custom protocol composition has not yet received an independent security audit.
- Group chats and calls are not production-ready.
- REALITY makes traffic resemble ordinary TLS. It is not an anonymity system and may not bypass every DPI policy; founder-run tests covered specific networks and dates.
- Sealed-sender-style envelopes reduce sender metadata, but the relay can still observe timing, message sizes, authenticated sessions and delivery destinations.

## What it does

- End-to-end encryption: a Double Ratchet implementation over libsodium, ED25519 identity keys generated on the device, X3DH session setup. The relay never sees plaintext; identity keys never leave the phone.
- Several ways to reach the network: Direct WSS (encrypted WebSocket over TLS), REALITY/Xray, Tor (v3 onion, text only) and a REST fallback for when WebSocket frames are silently dropped. When one route is blocked, another takes over. An offline mesh is planned (research stage).
- Three privacy modes: Standard (direct first, lowest latency), Private (REALITY first; not an anonymity mode), Ghost (Tor only; never silently downgrades, fails visibly instead; text only).
- Contact verification by mutual ED25519 fingerprint check and QR exchange. Encrypted voice notes.
- Fully open source: the code, the threat model, known issues and architecture decisions are public.

## Name

SHIFROM was previously called PHANTOM; the old site phntm.pro redirects here. It is not related to other products named Phantom.
